description: Agent harness for learning difficult things.

latest_release.body:
## Fixes

- Fix typing delays in answer and thinking fields during lessons.
- Fix Flashcards generation failing on OpenCode Go with `MissingSessionID`.
- Fix compaction overwriting newly saved skips, question dismissals, direction changes and pause state.
- Recover over-escaped code blocks while leaving normal code and mixed or incomplete fences unchanged.
- Read llama.cpp context limits from nested model metadata when necessary.
- Add common Nix profile directories to Claude Code discovery.

## Reading and performance

- Render Markdown, LaTeX and code in graph cards and expanded Chains statements. Proposition-name chips and source/folder labels in Chains remain plain text.
- Match inline-code size and colour to the surrounding graph-card and Chains statement text.
- Reposition graph cards as rendered content changes size.
- Allow wide tables to wrap to the available column where possible.
- Reduce repeated source-map file reads when building graph snapshots.

## Contributors

Thanks to @qrilka (#674), @MaxWang007 (#676), @SmitMachhi (#526), @Tang3n (#594), @wvlvrd (#516), @chryzsh (#570), @IsaacZhangg (#631, #648), @chirag-panjabi (#401), and @leoank (#574).

The code-fence recovery also uses a single-layer decoding approach proposed by @joneskim in #67.

detail.readme:
An agent harness for learning.

Download · How it works · Documentation · Issues · Discord

LearnHarness uses AI agents to plan and teach lessons from your current understanding to your goal. It builds a detailed picture of what you understand and how you reason. That picture is updated as you learn. Instead of just giving you an explanation, it uses your answers and thinking to decide what you need next. Teaching builds understanding one reasoning step at a time. Practice makes it usable. A persistent knowledge graph carries it across sessions. ![LearnHarness teaching session](docs/assets/teaching-session.png) ## How it works 1. **Measure.** Before teaching, the agent finds where your understanding ends on each part the lesson depends on. Your answers, confidence, and thinking show it where to start. 2. **Plan.** It works out a dependency map from that starting point to your goal. You can see the plan, and the lesson adapts when your understanding turns out different. 3. **Teach.** Each step builds on something you already understand. You predict, get an explanation, and check your understanding. Confusions are repaired before anything is built on them. The aim is for the goal to feel obviously true, not merely familiar. 4. **Practice.** Separate sessions pose varied problems that require the right knowledge to come to mind without being named first. Problems and hints adapt to your reasoning. **Think out loud.** The thinking fields let you explain your reasoning, uncertainties, and reactions in your own words. This is how the agent gets a detailed picture rather than just a record of right and wrong answers. You can type or use dictation. **Bring your files.** In the desktop app, attach PDFs, photos, or any other file with the paperclip, or drag them in. The file stays where it is: the message carries its path, and the agent reads it from there. The agent can also research questions in the background, create visual explanations, show your own images in the lesson and mark them up with arrows and labels, and build interactive demonstrations. ## Knowledge that carries forward What you are taught accumulates as propositions and reasoning chains: individual claims and the premises that lead to them. The graph shows this structure, with links back to the source sessions. You can also import notes. Future teaching sessions can read the graph instead of starting from scratch. Practice sessions can draw their material from it. It stores the ideas and their connections, not ratings of your ability. ![LearnHarness knowledge graph](docs/assets/knowledge-graph.png) ## Download and get started **[Download from learnharness.ai](https://learnharness.ai)** · [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/amosblomqvist/learnharness/releases) - **macOS (Apple Silicon):** signed and notarized DMG. Drag the app to Applications. - **Windows (x64):** run the installer. It is currently unsigned; Windows may show an “unknown publisher” or SmartScreen warning. - **Linux (x64):** make the AppImage executable and open it, or install the Debian/Ubuntu `.deb`. Choose your models, then start a session with what you want to understand. You can use provider API keys, supported subscription connections in the desktop app, an installed [Claude Code CLI](docs/claude-code.md), or a [custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint](docs/custom-providers.md), including a local model server. Optional dictation and web search use separate service keys. Web research can use a Tavily, Brave, Exa, Firecrawl, or Ollama key in Settings → Providers → Search. Ollama search uses its hosted service, not a local model server. See [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md) for model setup, dictation, files, and notes imports, and [context, caching, and costs](docs/compaction-accounting.md) for advanced cache preferences. All three platforms support in-app updates. ## Your keys, your data - **Your keys and models.** No LearnHarness subscription or markup. Billing depends on your provider, CLI configuration, subscription, or local setup. The live cost meter estimates known API costs, not subscription, CLI, or custom-endpoint charges. - **Local storage.** Your chats, graph, settings, and API keys live on your machine. Learning records are plain files you can inspect. - **External services.** Models run through your configured providers. Model requests send the context needed for the task; web research and dictation also contact external services. Local storage does not mean offline processing. - **Inspectable behavior.** System prompts are visible and editable. The app is open source under the AGPL-3.0 license. ## Development and support ```bash npm ci npm run plugins:setup npm run dev # http://localhost:3000 npm test # fixtures and fake providers ``` See the [documentation index](docs/README.md) for all guides, [development](docs/development.md) for setup and checks, [architecture](docs/architecture.md) for the runtime, [keyboard shortcuts](docs/keyboard.md), [themes](docs/themes.md) for the theme file format, and [desktop builds and releases](docs/desktop-release.md). For trusted local plugins, start with the [authoring guide and capability map](docs/plugin-authoring.md). It links the question, practice-problem, submission, view-context and UI contracts. Use [`examples/plugins/`](examples/plugins/) for small runnable templates, [`plugins/`](plugins/) for feature source projects, and the [host architecture](docs/plugin-architecture.md) for internals. Questions, bug reports, and feature requests: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/amosblomqvist/learnharness/issues). Security vulnerabilities: report privately as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), not in public issues. ## License [AGPL-3.0](LICENSE) The app is free and open forever. If we ever charge for anything, it will be for convenience — managed keys, hosting — never for features you can run locally.
